public_rationale: The records are consistent with limited aggregate employment effects and important comprehension weaknesses. They do not settle both parts of the claim. The employment study measures hiring and aggregate changes, not all jobs actually eliminated by AI. The language experiments demonstrate specific weaknesses, not an absence of comprehension across all October 2022 systems. Reduced hiring also prevents treating the employment evidence as showing no substitution.
limitations: Very few has no supplied numerical threshold.
The strongest employment evidence has narrower geographic and temporal coverage than the claim.
Benchmark failures do not establish a universal absence of understanding.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of October 2022, AI still lacks comprehension, and very few if any jobs have actually been replaced by AI.

statement.excerpt: Eleven years later, comprehension is still lacking (see any of my recent essays here) and very few if any jobs have actually been replaced by AI.
statement.document_title: Three baffling claims about AI and machine learning in four days, statistical errors in top journals, and claims from Yann LeCun that you should not believe.

our_interpretation: The statement combines two propositions: AI still lacked robust general comprehension, and actual replacement of human jobs by AI remained rare.
In context, comprehension means understanding language and situations across unfamiliar settings, rather than succeeding on an isolated language benchmark.
Jobs means human employment positions. Automating tasks, reducing hiring, and eliminating an entire occupation are different outcomes.
I read very few as a small share of employment, without inventing a numerical cutoff or restricting the claim to one country.

The target interval follows the explicit comparison with 2011. Job replacement is cumulative through the post; comprehension concerns the endpoint. Earlier comprehension tests are context rather than direct measurements of the October endpoint.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence shows that actual AI-caused job displacement remained small through October 16, 2022, and broad evaluations of systems existing then show substantial failures of general comprehension.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes substantial actual job replacement attributable to AI during the interval, or an existing system demonstrates robust general comprehension across unfamiliar settings. Isolated job losses do not alone contradict very few.

evidence.explanation: The study reports reduced hiring at exposed establishments and no detectable aggregate employment relationship in its earlier US data. Neither finding counts gross jobs eliminated worldwide through October 2022; available_at conservatively uses the last day of the stated February 2022 revision month.

evidence.locator: Section 3, discussion of Figure 11 and cause-and-effect task formulations
evidence.explanation: The experiments show that success on one formulation of a causal-language task need not transfer to another. This supports concern about robustness, but a June evaluation of selected models does not establish an October-wide absence of comprehension.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative historical estimate of actual AI-caused job displacement through the post, plus broad evaluations of the systems available then under an explicit, ordinary comprehension standard.
